LENA VARGA-HOLM
Senior Data Engineer
Rijeka, Croatia (open to remote, EU time zones) | lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101 | github.com/lvh-data-example

PROFILE
Data engineer with 9 years of experience building batch and streaming data platforms for e-commerce and payments. I like boring, well-tested pipelines, clear data contracts and warehouses that analysts actually trust.

EXPERIENCE

Senior Data Engineer - Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. (logistics marketplace), Rijeka            03/2022 - present
- Own the ingestion layer of the company data platform: ~140 Airflow DAGs loading from Postgres, MySQL, Salesforce and 3rd-party APIs into Snowflake.
- Moved transformation logic from stored procedures to dbt (420+ models, tests on every model); nightly run time down from 5h10 to 1h35.
- Introduced data contracts between product teams and the data team (JSON Schema + CI checks), cutting broken-pipeline incidents from ~9/month to ~2/month.
- Built a Kafka-based event pipeline (Kafka Connect + Snowpipe Streaming) for shipment tracking events, ~30M events/day.
- Mentor two mid-level data engineers; run the weekly data platform office hours.

Data Engineer - Kovalent Pay (payments startup), Zagreb                            09/2019 - 02/2022
- Built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR for transaction reconciliation (daily ~1.2 TB of raw files from S3).
- Designed the Redshift warehouse schema (star schema, 30+ fact/dimension tables) used by finance and risk.
- Set up data quality checks with Great Expectations on critical finance tables.
- Wrote internal Python library for S3/Glue catalog access used by 4 teams.

Junior Data Engineer / BI Developer - Adria Retail Group, Split                     06/2017 - 08/2019
- Maintained SSIS packages and T-SQL ETL into an on-prem SQL Server warehouse.
- Built Power BI reports for store operations (40+ stores).
- Migrated 60 nightly SSIS jobs to Python scripts scheduled with cron.

EDUCATION
MSc Computer Science (Data Science track) - Northgate Technical University, 2017
Thesis: Incremental materialized views for analytical queries

CERTIFICATIONS
AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate (May 2024)

SKILLS
Languages: Python, SQL, Bash
Data: Airflow, dbt, Spark (PySpark), Kafka, Kafka Connect, Snowflake, Redshift, PostgreSQL, Great Expectations
Cloud & infra: AWS (S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM), Docker, Terraform (basic), GitHub Actions
BI: Power BI, Looker (basic)

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native), English (C1), German (B1)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise senior-level CV with clear progression, credible production scale, and excellent quantified outcomes. The experience bullets demonstrate ownership of data-platform components, performance improvements, reliability work, mentoring, and relevant fintech exposure. The structure is professional and easy to scan. The main content weakness is that several highly relevant achievements in the candidate information are absent: on-call operation, Snowflake cost optimisation, Debezium CDC, open-source contributions, and measurable reconciliation impact. The profile phrase “I like boring” is personable but slightly informal for a senior application and could be replaced with more professional language focused on reliable, maintainable platforms.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses conventional section headings, reverse-chronological experience, plain text formatting, and keyword-rich bullets, so it should parse reliably in most ATS systems. It contains strong matches for Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Snowflake, Redshift, Spark, Kafka, Docker, CI/CD, data quality, and dimensional modelling. Estimated AI/ATS screening probability is high for the core Senior Data Engineer requirements. Screening could improve further by explicitly using the job's terms “production data platform,” “query optimisation,” “data modelling,” “open-source,” “data governance,” and “operating/on-call,” where supported by the candidate's material. The current CV does not show the candidate's open-source contribution or explicitly connect the large-scale data work to query/performance optimisation.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with the central role: the candidate owns part of a production data platform, operates Airflow and Snowflake pipelines, has large-scale streaming and batch experience, uses dbt and Docker, and has payments-domain experience. The 1.2 TB daily workload, 30 million events per day, 420+ dbt models, and warehouse runtime reduction are particularly persuasive. Strong data modelling is shown through the Redshift star schema and fact/dimension tables. AWS is a credible comparable cloud experience through S3, EMR, Glue, Redshift, Snowflake, Docker, and related services, although the candidate has no Google Cloud experience. The CV also supports the company's ownership and collaborative culture through platform ownership, mentoring, office hours, data contracts, and work with product teams. Missing evidence includes explicit query optimisation on large datasets, open-source practices, and the candidate's operational on-call responsibility. Graph modelling and Portuguese are gaps based on the supplied candidate material; these should not be presented as document defects.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / JOB-ALIGNMENT ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Experience section under “Senior Data Engineer - Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o.”, add a bullet using the candidate's documented operational responsibility: “Participate in the data-platform on-call rotation (1 week in 6), diagnosing and resolving production pipeline incidents.” This will directly support the requirement to build and operate a production data platform.
2. In the same Lukovac experience section, add the documented Snowflake performance and cost result: “Optimised Snowflake warehouse sizing, auto-suspend settings and unused-table retention, reducing monthly spend from approximately $38K to $24K in 2024.” This provides concrete evidence of optimisation at scale and ownership of platform efficiency.
3. In the same section, add the documented CDC achievement: “Replaced hourly full-table extracts from PostgreSQL with Debezium CDC into Kafka, reducing replica CPU during loads from approximately 70% to 25%.” Include “Debezium” in the Skills section under Data or Streaming because it is a relevant ATS keyword supported by the candidate's material.
4. In the Professional Experience section under “Data Engineer - Kovalent Pay,” strengthen the existing reconciliation bullet with the documented business outcome: “Built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR to reconcile approximately 1.2 TB of daily S3 files against internal ledgers, reducing finance-team month-end reconciliation from approximately 3 days to 4 hours.”
5. In the Professional Summary or the relevant experience bullets, explicitly use “query optimisation” only in connection with the supported Snowflake and warehouse performance work. For example: “Senior Data Engineer with 9 years of experience designing, building and operating production data platforms and cloud data warehouses, including Python/SQL query optimisation, batch and streaming pipelines, data quality, and dimensional modelling.” Do not claim a tool or technique not documented in the candidate information.
6. Add a short “OPEN-SOURCE AND COMMUNITY” section after Certifications, containing only documented evidence: “Contributor, community Airflow provider: fixed a pagination bug, added tests, and merged 2 pull requests (2023).” You may also include: “Speaker, ‘Data contracts without the hype,’ regional data meetup (2024)” and “SQL instructor, local Women in Tech meetup, approximately 4 evenings per year since 2021.” This directly supports the ad's open-source and collaboration signals.

MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
7. In the Profile section, replace the informal sentence “I like boring, well-tested pipelines, clear data contracts and warehouses that analysts actually trust” with a more professional version such as: “Focused on reliable, well-tested pipelines, clear data contracts, and trusted analytical warehouses.”
8. In the Skills section, change “Terraform (basic)” to “Terraform” only if the candidate wants to avoid an unnecessarily weakening label; otherwise retain the honest proficiency qualifier. Add “Debezium” and “pytest” only because both are supported by the candidate's portfolio and notes.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured senior data engineering CV. critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, reverse-chronological experience, standard text formatting, searchable technology names, and no problematic tables, graphics, or unconventional layout elements. critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns very well with the role. The payments experience and finance/risk warehouse work are particularly relevant to Halden Pay. The candidate also demonstrates ownership, collaboration, knowledge sharing, and pace through on-call work, incident reduction, mentoring, office hours, and measurable runtime improvements. Graph modelling is a gap in the candidate material, and Portuguese is a gap; neither is a document defect. Explicit SQL query optimisation at large-dataset scale is not clearly evidenced in the original material, so the CV should avoid overstating that point and instead describe the directly supported warehouse, runtime, and cost optimisation work.
critique.improvement_instructions:

If the candidate has genuinely performed SQL query optimisation, it should be described with a concrete example and metric in the relevant Experience bullet; otherwise, do not claim it.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, highly credible senior-level CV. It is concise, well structured, professional, and focused on production data engineering rather than generic responsibilities. The profile establishes relevant scope across batch and streaming platforms, cloud warehouses, data quality, modelling, and reliability. Experience bullets use strong metrics, including 140 Airflow DAGs, 420+ dbt models, 30M events per day, runtime reduction, incident reduction, and Snowflake cost savings. The CV also effectively demonstrates ownership, mentoring, operational responsibility, and business impact. The AWS certification, open-source contribution, technical talk, and teaching activity strengthen seniority and professional credibility.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional headings, chronological experience, plain text formatting, standard date ranges, and clear technology lists. It contains strong matches for Airflow, dbt, Python, SQL, Docker, CI/CD, Kafka, Snowflake, AWS, data quality, dimensional modelling, and data platforms. AI screening probability is high because the document contains both relevant keywords and concrete evidence of scale and outcomes. The main minor opportunity is to surface a few additional supported technical terms from the candidate material—especially incremental dbt models, slim CI/state:modified workflows, AWS MSK, dead-letter/replay tooling, and latency—rather than leaving them only in the portfolio information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very strongly with Halden Pay's Data Platform role. It shows experience designing, building, and operating a production data platform; owning ingestion and orchestration; working with Airflow and dbt; enforcing data contracts and data quality; operating Snowflake and Redshift warehouses; and supporting payments-related reconciliation and risk data. AWS is a credible comparable cloud experience through S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM, Snowflake, Docker, and Terraform. The open-source contribution, data architecture talk, mentoring, office hours, and cross-team data contracts support the advertised curiosity, collaboration, ownership, and learning orientation. The CV does not show graph modelling or Portuguese, which are listed as nice-to-have requirements. It also does not establish experience with the employer's specific Google Cloud stack, but the AWS experience is directly relevant as comparable cloud experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
Minor enhancement — In the Experience section under Lukovac Freight Hub, expand the Kafka/Snowpipe Streaming bullet with supported operational detail from the candidate portfolio: add that the pipeline achieved end-to-end latency under 2 minutes at p95 and included a dead-letter topic and replay tooling for failed events. For example: "Built a Kafka-based event pipeline (Kafka Connect + Snowpipe Streaming) for shipment tracking events, processing ~30M events/day with end-to-end latency under 2 minutes at p95; added dead-letter and replay tooling to reprocess failed events without data loss."

Minor enhancement — In the existing dbt bullet under Lukovac Freight Hub, add the supported architecture and CI terms from the portfolio: "incremental models," "slim CI," "state:modified," and "GitHub Actions." For example: "Moved transformation logic from stored procedures to dbt, migrating 420+ models with tests and documentation; introduced incremental models and slim CI using state:modified in GitHub Actions, reducing nightly runtime from 5h10 to 1h35."
